answer: Proof-of-stake mechanisms anchor Sybil resistance to capital rather than ephemeral identity, treating compute-units like copper in a circuit. An attacker must bond significant assets, similar to the foundational stability of a basalt cliff, to participate. If the network is an international wharf for data exchange, this cost-to-validate forces agents to possess verified economic skin-in-the-game, rendering the creation of infinite low-cost malicious identities prohibitively expensive and strictly non-profitable.
